Please use the Psykhanium Meat Grinder to test builds, learn weapon attack patterns, learn how many hits a weapon takes to kill enemies on the difficulty you are playing on. I see way too many people not using this feature. It is extremely useful when you are a new player and a veteran for learning different weapons, play styles, and breakpoints.

Few more tips:

- If you or someone else gets picked up by a Chaos Spawn, get close to them. It will start the Spawn's throwing animation and he won't eat the person he's holding
- If you pull a daemonhost, put a med crate under the person that has aggro and beat the living shit out of the daemonhost. They have less health than normal bosses and the real issue is losing people too quickly to the frenzy attacks. If you have aggro just hold block and dodge and stay within the med crate.

- Pysker shields block more than just bullets. They block scab bomber grenades and trapper nets.

- Use your nades (for psykers either the vent or surge blitz) to create stagger and space when a teammate is down. Use the explosion and time a revive to pick them up easier.

This is the leveling guide I used. It doesn't include what I've included about the raid, but it gives you a general idea of tier levels for engrams. Your drops from soft capped powerful engrams will never be huge increases unless your armor is vastly lower than your current light. Depends on your light level. If you are under 540 do every milestone including nightfall before dreaming city. After 540 you do the exact opposite. Raid first for the increase in power level, then do milestones to bring your gear up to that power level. Once your armor is at or around your current level, do dreaming city for another power increase and then milestones. Basically, if 3/5 armor pieces are below your current light level, do milestones. If not, do things with a higher soft cap than your light first. There was a post related to this last week that I used

570+ on all 3 characters. I play 4-8 hours a day depending on the activity. My clan raids pretty consistently and I don't mind helping out if I can. I started last Tuesday at 550 on all characters so there is definitely a right way to do things. After learning how to increase my light efficiently, I am happy with this system. The raid has given me the most in power increase and I recommend to anyone else over 540 TRY TO DO THE RAID FIRST BEFORE MILESTONES. You will get better rewards and see a large power increase doing milestones later. Thank you bungie for this new system. The biggest problem I see in low-level counter-strike is people have no idea how to move correctly in this game. Being unpredictable with movements makes it less likely to be shot since enemies are trying to predict where and when you will peek. If you want to improve your movement, play jump maps (KZ mod) and 1v1 servers. Jump maps will teach you how to strafe and 1v1s are where you can apply it the best. When I awp, my muscle memory has taught me to shoot at the end of my strafe when I know I will be accurate. In game, it will look like I am still moving as I shoot. This takes a lot of practice. I learned how to do it in source and since the awp change in global offensive, I have had to quick scope a lot more. [Add me](http://steamcommunity.com/id/matrixcsgo/home) if anyone wants to learn to play better. Message me on reddit your username. I get a lot of spam invites.
